reviews.review_description:
Nothing about this version of HTVR is any different than the free tests BBL has done: we’re still fighting the same handful of enemies in the same desert with the same four classes. The only difference is that it costs money in ways that feel underhanded.

The game wants to be a roguelite but its contents do not support the replayability required to be one. Each 30-ish minute ‘run’ tours through a few levels ending with the final boss (of which there is only one). At the end of each level, you’ll choose which one to go to next, but they’re all so same-y that it doesn’t matter—you’ll fight waves of skeletons regardless. The combat is bland too—each character works in a simplistic way that cannot be altered: the knight swings a sword, the archer shoots arrows, the mage throws potions, and the brawler punches. Outside of basic stat buffs, that’s it. Every run plays the same; there aren’t choices to make between levels, upgrades, or playstyles, there aren’t challenges to work around, ways to cooperate with teammates, or skills to master. You pick a character that applies damage in one of four ways, and stick it out until the final boss again and again.

There are hidden costs in the game: “Want to go through this door? $12! Want to wear a hat? $4! Want to play again? That’ll cost too!” This was never how the game was advertised. Why not charge up-front? I’ve seen responses to other reviews where the devs state they’re tuning prices, but they’re charging players now. The time to test was *before* it was for sale. It’s on BBL to make something that’s worth the time and money they’re asking for, no amount of ‘we’re listening to feedback’ replaces that.

The most fun I had with HTVR was laughing as a kid left my party because they “just got Chinese food, and it honestly smells like more fun.” I have beaten the campaign with every class and tried everything the game has to offer. I want this to be good but what’s being offered is just too bland and simple.

developer_response.body: Thank you for taking the time to write this, and for playing through with every class first. You’re right that replayability is what a roguelite lives on, and points like run variety, meaningful choices between levels, and ways to cooperate with teammates are exactly what we want to dig into during Early Access. We hear your frustration with the in-game purchases too, and we’ve passed that along to the team. If you’re open to it, we’d love to hear more in our Discord: https://discord.gg/5KG86mKUFE. (To be fair, the Chinese food line made us laugh too)

reviews.review_title: Solid but could use some spice
reviews.review_description:
The game is solid if a little basic right now, some more fleshed-out roguelike elements would go a long way.

I've played the campaign through with all the different heroes and upgraded all their weapons, and right now I feel like each run mostly plays out the same/lacks uniqueness that would make playing through multiple times more engaging. Each hero is fun to mess around with, but they feel fairly one-note, and there aren't options in the game as of now to tweak them to play differently or adapt to enemies/levels/situations. The Knight, Archer, and Mage all work well and feel balanced (I did have some frustration with the hit detection on the Brawler and felt that maybe that hero's attack range could be increased a bit to avoid getting hit by accident in CQB) but they don't have much room for mastery or skill expression. I feel like a good fit might be MOBA-style ability sets on cooldowns or deeper interactions with each other and the environment: maybe the Mage could cast elemental spells on the Knight's sword or Archer's arrows, or the Knight could carry a shield that the Brawler could pick up and throw at enemies Captain America-style, or weather events like thunderstorms or heatwaves could strengthen certain enemies and debuff certain attacks. A handful of these sorts of options would make the game feel a bit more mysterious and serve as a hook to keep doing runs/experimenting with the cast of heroes.

Maybe what I'm suggesting isn't quite what Heroes Together is going for, and if so, fair enough. What's here is fun, I just want to have more of a reason jump back in and keep playing.

Wishing the team luck on the road to the full release!

developer_response.body: Thank you for such a thoughtful review! The note on Brawler hit detection and range is really useful, and ideas like Mage spells on the Knight's sword or a throwable shield are exactly the kind of thing we love hearing. We can't promise what will or won't make it in, but feedback like this shapes where Early Access goes. Thanks for the well wishes!

reviews.review_description:
done a few dungeons already though I've found that the mage's fire and ice spells are Unpredictable when i yeet them at a enemy,

 the knight's beam sword projectile is also a little random(not always shooting out when i either swing or thrust the sword forward,

Finally i actually don't know if its the game or my quest but after completing a run with both sudden death and the time limit challenges on the game just crashed and now i cant even play it anymore.

Complete with preparations for (yet another) predatory cash shop. 🤣

Timer on dungeon entries (temporarily waylaid) is an instant red flag, and foreshadows a P2P (and ultimately a P2W) format.

Yes, early access, hence the middle-ground rating, and we'll see where it goes over time.

The Power Stances are a unique touch, making emoting in-game an advantageous mechanic, add some much needed flavor to the pot, and pretty much saves the game from being completely mundane.

That said, unless you enjoy Wii levels of combat depth, do yourself and whatever kids would be playing a favor, and pay for a game with some mechanics more significant than waggling (or pointing and clicking) at mostly brainless mobs.

developer_response.body: Thanks for giving HTVR a fair shot, and for the honest take. We’re glad Power Poses stood out, since playing together is at the heart of what we’re building. Your feedback on the dungeon timer and combat depth has been noted, and Early Access is where we shape the game with our players. If you’re up for it, tell us what deeper combat would look like to you in our Discord: https://discord.gg/tR4tmvyNU. We read everything.

reviews.review_title: Good for a early access free game
reviews.review_description:
Visuals: 8/10 better then most free games , the same as the trailer
Physics: 6/10 the bows are good, but the sword doesn’t interact with anything
Enemies: 8/10 they are dumb, but are interesting and still fun to fight
Bosses: 9/10 the bosses are really fun and a challenge, one of my favorite parts of the game
Puzzles: 7/10 there are some basic puzzles (like different colored gates and one person controls the levers) that require teamwork that are fun but relatively easy
Overall: 8/10, it shows potential and is pretty fun.

For the devs: this is a really good game and I would appreciate it if you made a discord server for recommendations for enemies, bosses, spells, etc. Update: I found the server on the website

developer_response.body: Love the full breakdown, and glad the bosses are a favourite! Thanks for flagging the sword interactions too. We actually do have a Discord with a suggestions channel, so feel free to drop your enemy, boss, and spell ideas in there anytime: https://discord.gg/5KG86mKUFE

reviews.review_title: not bad at all : early access review.
reviews.review_description:
graphics : 3.5/ 5 about what you would expect from the trailers, and from the style of game.
 gameplay : 4/5 really good bow physics and things react the way you would expect and just work. 
Accessibility : all movement options are here. I didn't look for blinders or see that in the menu, but snap turn smooth turn teleport and smooth walking are all present. 
All in all it's a good experience for an early access free game. It's no dungeons of Eternity but it's not trying to be either. This feels like it's going to be a social experience that happens to be a game more than a game with social experience but either way I'm excited to see where it goes.
